div.div: Required: every method reachable from the frontend needs @api.model. Without it the call fails at dispatch, and the browser console error does not name the missing decorator.

div.p: showDeliveryCreationDateColumn hides the creation_date definition when state.active_preset is today. Since header and row cells both iterate deliveryColumns, the column is removed consistently and returns in its saved drag position for other presets. The empty-state cell uses the visible column count. No backend filtering is changed.
div.h3: Version 18.0.10.11.28 — Delivery customer mobile and draggable columns
div.p: _operations_picking_row() adds partner_mobile to the picking payload, using the direct delivery partner mobile and then its commercial partner's mobile as a fallback. DELIVERY_COLUMN_DEFINITIONS is the authoritative label/key/sort mapping for the Delivery Orders table. Both its header and each row iterate the reactive deliveryColumnOrder list, so column reordering updates headers and cells together instead of manually moving DOM nodes. The order persists in eagle_operations_delivery_column_order_v1. Each column key maps to an accessor in OPERATIONS_SORT_ACCESSORS.deliveries.
div.h3: Version 18.0.10.11.27 — Quick Internal Transfer dropdown defaults
div.p: EagleQuickInternalTransferDialog.open() no longer preloads suggestions or causes all three dropdowns to open on launch. Suggestions are fetched on explicit input clicks or typing; focus changes by the wizard do not open dropdowns.
div.h3: Version 18.0.10.11.26 — Operations sorting and default folding
div.p: Quotations, RFQ, Transactions, Delivery Orders, Receiving Orders, and Internal Stock Transfer start folded by default and sort each displayed column through an explicit per-table field map. The handler validates field keys, updates Owl state, and persists sort direction. Comparisons treat numeric fields as numbers, dates chronologically, keep empty values at the end, and use deterministic tie-breaking. The fold-state namespace is eagle_operations_managed_fold_v4_*, which resets prior open-state preferences on upgrade. All Operations tables remain marked data-eagle-managed-controls="1" so generic DOM-only table handlers cannot override the component state.

table_tools.js standardizes fold/sort behavior across Business, Finance and Operations. A new table preference namespace means all tables initialize folded once after upgrade. It binds title controls only for single-table cards; multi-table and nested cards receive per-table controls. Existing component-owned fold controls and the reactive Operations Orders/Purchase sorting remain authoritative.
div.h3: Version 18.0.10.11.22 — Shared Quick Sale and table controls
div.p: Both dashboard.js and operations_dashboard.js instantiate the shared EagleQuickSaleDialog from quick_sale_dialog.js. The previous Business Dashboard-only inline modal was removed, so partner lookup, product lookup, validation, and creation behavior are identical on both pages. Each caller supplies its own post-create refresh callback.

table_tools.js provides common click-to-sort behavior for generic headings and persists/reapplies sort direction for the Owl-managed Business/Finance transaction headers too. Table preferences use stable card-title/column-label keys rather than a page-wide table index, preventing preferences from shifting when a panel is conditionally rendered.
Each screen is a client action. The pattern, repeated for all five components:
The tag is matched by an ir.actions.client record in views/menu.xml.

setup() builds useState and the month/year option lists; onWillStart fetches the first payload; onMounted starts the presence heartbeat timer; onWillDestroy clears it. Any timer you add must be cleared in onWillDestroy or it keeps firing after the user navigates away.

Drill-down goes through open_dynamic_action, which creates an action server-side and returns its id. The frontend then opens /odoo/action-{id} in a new tab. This exists because a dynamic domain cannot be expressed as a static xmlid.

manuals.js defines a ManualBase class holding the sidebar search, section switching, print and dark-mode toggles; UserManual and DeveloperManual extend it and supply a static sections array. To add a topic, add one entry to that array and one t-if block to the matching XML template - nothing else.
shared_filter_state.js exports a plain mutable object imported by all three dashboards. It is a module-scope singleton, not an Odoo service.
div.pre: from_date, to_date, partner_filter, active_preset, selected_month, selected_year
div.p: On setup() a component seeds its useState from the singleton. Before navigating away it calls its _syncShared() helper to push current values back. The next screen therefore opens with the same filters.
div.div: State lives in browser memory only - a page reload resets it to defaults. Anything that must survive a reload belongs in dashboard.saved.filter instead.

div.p: get_product_options() returns id and label pairs to populate the searchable dropdown. This exists because an earlier build required users to type a raw database id, which is not usable UX. Never reintroduce an id-entry field.

create_quick_sale searches for an existing draft sale.order for the partner. If one exists the line is appended to it; otherwise a new draft is created. This prevents a pile of one-line drafts per customer.

price_unit is optional. When omitted, Odoo's own pricelist resolution applies; when supplied it overrides. Failures are returned to the frontend as a message rather than raised as a traceback, so the panel can show a readable error under the button.

The frequently-bought-together panel. It pairs products co-occurring on the same order and ranks pairs by frequency. Raw SQL is used rather than the ORM because the self-join over order lines is far cheaper in SQL.

A 30-day projection built from posted invoices and bills with due dates in the window. It is arithmetic on existing documents, not a statistical forecast - do not describe it to users as a prediction of future sales.
Both compare current figures against historical aggregates. They are indicative and intended to prompt a human check.
One-click completion for sale and purchase orders, plus the extended payment validation. Entry point: complete_order(model, record_id).
sale.order and purchase.order only. Anything else raises a UserError rather than guessing.
div.pre:
1. Confirm draft|sent|to approve sale -> action_confirm() purchase -> button_confirm() failure here aborts - later stages need a confirmed order
2. Transfers order.picking_ids, state not in (done, cancel) action_assign() move.quantity = move.product_uom_qty; move.picked = True button_validate() wizard action dict -> create({}) then process()
3. Invoice sale invoice_status == 'to invoice' -> _create_invoices() purchase invoice_status == 'to invoice' -> action_create_invoice()
4. Post draft invoice_ids -> action_post() vendor bills get invoice_date = today first
div.p: Every stage - and every individual picking - runs inside self.env.cr.savepoint(). A stage that raises is rolled back to its savepoint and appended to warnings; stages that already succeeded stand. This is deliberate: a short-stock delivery should not discard a confirmation that worked.
The return payload is {id, name, state, invoice_status, steps, warnings}. The frontend shows steps as what happened and warnings as what stopped short.
Every stage tests its own state before acting, so the method is safe to call repeatedly. This is what lets the user press Process again after fixing a blockage rather than having to unpick anything.

get_dashboard attaches a can_process boolean to every row in quotations, orders, purchases and rfq. It is true when the state is still open, the invoice status is to invoice, a picking is outstanding, or a draft invoice exists. The template shows the button on can_process alone - never compute this in the template.

validate_payment now drives the Odoo 18 chain draft -> in_process -> paid. A draft is posted with action_post(); an in_process payment is then advanced with action_validate(), guarded by hasattr because that method is not present on every Odoo 18 build. The template shows the Validate button for both draft and in_process.
div.pre: _eagle_fill_picking_quantities(picking) set done qty from demand _eagle_validate_picking(picking) validate + answer wizards _eagle_post_invoices(invoices) post drafts, date vendor bills _eagle_err(exc) one-line readable message
div.p: These are plain methods, not @api.model - they are internal and must not be reachable by RPC.
div.div: Irreversible: stages 2 and 4 move stock and post accounting entries. Any change here needs testing on a database copy first, never straight on the live instance.

div.p: create_snapshot_link(snapshot_dict, hours) serialises the current figures to JSON in snapshot_data and returns a token. The controller looks the token up with sudo(), checks expires_at, and renders snapshot_view - or snapshot_expired when missing or lapsed. JSON parsing is wrapped in try/except and falls back to an empty dict, so a corrupt blob renders an empty page rather than a 500.
div.div: Security: this route is auth='public' and uses sudo(). The token is the only control. Never widen what the snapshot payload contains without considering that it is readable by anyone holding the URL, and keep default expiry short.

div.pre: id: cron_daily_digest model: dashboard.data code: model.send_daily_digest() interval: 1 day active: False (off on install, by design)
div.p: Wrapped in <data noupdate="1"> so a module upgrade does not re-disable a job the customer switched on. toggle_daily_digest(enabled) flips active; get_digest_status() reports it.
The digest body is built with Python f-strings and sent through mail.mail directly, not through a mail.template.
div.div: Mako ${...} syntax is not rendered in Odoo 17/18 mail templates. This is why the digest bypasses templates entirely. Do not "improve" it back into a mail.template.
The numbercall field was removed in Odoo 18. Adding it to an ir.cron record raises on install.

div.pre: group_dashboard_user KPI cards and summary tables group_dashboard_manager + analytics, operations, customers group_dashboard_admin everything + visibility configuration
div.p: All three sit in base.module_category_hidden so they do not clutter the user form's application list.

dashboard.data is read-only to base.group_user - correct, since it is abstract and stores nothing. Personal models (saved filters, snoozes, presence, comments, snapshot links) grant full CRUD to base.group_user, with record-level ir.rule restricting each user to their own rows. dashboard.approval.config is readable by all and writable only by group_dashboard_admin.
The Developer Manual menu carries groups="base.group_system", so it is invisible to non-administrators. The User Manual menu has no group restriction.
div.div: Menu visibility is not data security. It hides the entry; it does not stop a determined user from triggering the client action tag. Keep genuinely sensitive content out of the manual templates.

div.p: Adding a KPI card touches four places, in this order.

ol.li: Backend. Add the figure to the relevant get_* method's return dict in dashboard.py, or add a new @api.model method if it is expensive and should load separately.
Component state. Add the key to useState with a sensible zero value so the first render has something to show, and assign it where the payload is applied.
Template. Add the card markup, reusing eagle-kpi-card plus a colour class such as kpi-blue. For a clickable card add the clickable class and a _newTab(...) handler.
Both manuals. Describe the card in the User Manual and, if you added a method, list it in the RPC reference here.

div.div: Computed values belong in a JS getter, not in the template. The OWL expression parser rejects ?? and Math.max(...arr). The existing animOverdueCount and trendMax getters exist for exactly this reason.

div.p: One stylesheet, dashboard.css, serves all five screens. Everything is scoped under .eagle-app, and dark mode is the .dark class on that same root.
div.pre:
--eagle-accent user-chosen accent, injected inline via themeStyle
.eagle-app root, owns the accent variable .eagle-header sticky gradient header .eagle-body scrolling region .eagle-kpi-grid auto-fit grid, min 190px .eagle-kpi-card + kpi-blue | kpi-green | kpi-red ... .eagle-manual-* manual shell: wrap, side, navbtn, content, table, code
div.p: The accent colour is applied as an inline custom property from the themeStyle getter rather than written into the stylesheet, so it can vary per user. Use var(--eagle-accent) in new rules instead of hardcoding the default blue.
Breakpoint is 768px. Check any new panel there before shipping - the dashboards are used on phones.
Each of these cost real debugging time. Read before writing templates, crons, mail or XML.

tr.td: No ??, no Math.max(...spread) in templates. Move the logic to a JS getter.
Deprecated in Odoo 18 cron. Remove it from ir.cron records.
${...} is not rendered in 17/18 templates. Use f-strings with mail.mail.
Needs a UTF-8 declaration and numeric HTML entities, not raw bytes.
Required on every get_* and action method called from the frontend.
The presence heartbeat can collide. Wrap in a savepoint with a fallback.
Odoo 18 uses <list>, not <tree>. Use inline invisible= expressions.

div.p: Known and accepted, not bugs. Recorded so the next person does not rediscover them.

tr.td: N+1 queries - sales history fetched per product
One grouped read_group over all candidates, then compute in Python
N+1 - iterates day by day with a query each
Single query grouped by day, then walk the result
N+1 - per-vendor aggregates in a loop
Aggregate in one SQL pass keyed by partner

div.p: All three are acceptable at current data volume. Revisit when product or vendor counts grow, or if dashboard load time becomes noticeable.
Every generated build bumps both the version in __manifest__.py and the version suffix in the zip filename, and the two must match:
Sequential zips are the recovery path - the development filesystem has been lost more than once, and the version chain is what made rollback possible. Keep every zip.

ol.li: Back up the database before anything else.
Unzip into the addons path, replacing the existing eagle_business_dashboard folder.
Delete stale __pycache__ directories.
Restart the Odoo service.
Apps, remove the Apps filter, search the module, Upgrade.
Hard-refresh the browser so the asset bundle is rebuilt - a stale bundle looks exactly like broken JS.

div.div: A changed asset list in the manifest requires the upgrade, not just a restart. Symptoms of skipping it: new template not found, or a client action tag that does not resolve.

div.p: Run through this before generating the zip. Prefer one comprehensive pass over several small iterations.

ol.li: Manifest version bumped, zip filename suffix matches it.
Any new file added to the manifest data or assets list, in the right position.
New models have an ir.model.access.csv line.
New frontend-callable methods carry @api.model.
No ?? or spread in templates; computed values in getters.
New XML is ASCII, or declares UTF-8 and uses numeric entities.
New timers cleared in onWillDestroy.
New panel checked at the 768px breakpoint and in dark mode.
User Manual updated for anything a user can see or click.
Developer Manual updated for structure, models, RPC methods or gotchas.
Version string in both manual footers updated.
